page.layout: One text column with marginal notes in the left margin: "Cauda Draconis," beside the first paragraph, "Eclipsis," beside the Eclipsis paragraph, and "SOL." beside the Majus paragraph. Running head at top, page number 88 at top left, catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: Cauda Draconis,Inferior seu cauda Draconis est punctum illud, ubi Luna ab Ecliptica digrediens Austrum versus descendit.
Totalis est totius diametri nobis apparentis in luminari.
Partialis est unius vel aliquot partium, seu Digitorum.
Digitus hoc loco est duodecima luminaris pars.

SOL.Majus est Planeta, qui praeest diei, diciturq; Sol, ac est luminare majus, seu Planeta omnium maximus & lucidissimus, calorem vivificum cum luce mundo impertiens, motu communi seu diurno diem, proprio & periodico annum & vices temporum efficiens.
Sol dicitur Lucis sedes & vehiculum, luce lucens propria & nativa. Magnitudo lucis est tanta, ut Universum mundum repleat, & radios ad mundi extrema mittat; Copia tanta est, ut alia fidera obscuret.

page.notes: The marginal notes are small italic and in the left margin. The long s is written as s throughout. The running head SECVNDI is written SECUNDI under the u/v rule. Some faded show-through from the reverse side is visible on the right and was left out. The line "vertente,scilicet dies 36 5 ." was read as 365. The line at the foot ends with the catchword "qua-", which was not repeated in the text. The italic line "Luminare est Majus vel Minus." was read as a set-apart subheading.
